paragraphs.text: # dsh-context-diet

A DeepSeek Harness (DSH) bundle that **elides stale, oversized tool results from the
model-visible s
ession surface** and shows what it saved in the composer footer.

It is a port of pi-context-diet
(MIT, Copyright (c) 2026 sorinirimies) to DSH's durable session-surf

ace model. The
policy core is a line-by-line port; the adapter translates DSH events into the
messag
e shapes that core expects.

The goal is not only fewer tokens. A long session re-sends build logs, file dumps
and exploration no

ise on every step, and that noise competes with the material the
model actually needs. Removing it w

hen the prompt cache is already cold keeps the
working set small and the model focused, at no cache

he prompt cache is already cold keeps the
working set small and the model focused, at no cache cost.

- Status: **enabled by default**, Host + Client bundle, no build step.
- Version anchor: developed a
gainst `@deepseek-ai/dsh` **0.2.1-rc.5**.
## What it does

At the pre-step phase the plugin looks at the current session surface, and when the
prompt cache is

cold — the last assistant message is older than `cacheTtlMinutes` —
it replaces old, large, plain-te
xt `tool/result` nodes with a deterministic stub.

A stub keeps the tool identity, the original size, a few tail lines and any error
lines, so an exit
status or a failure survives:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

The replacement is a 1:1 durable `tool/result` surface replacement
(`surfaceOp: { op: 'replace', sta

rtSeq, endSeq }`, `sourceEventSeqs: [seq]`),
preceded by the native pruner's log-only `compaction/pr

une` shadow price. The
original event stays in the log; only the model-visible copy is shorter.
## The footer
The composer footer shows the same three facts pi's status line shows:
| State | Text |

| Nothing elided yet | `🥗 −12.4k at the next pause` (what the next cold start would drop) |
| Nothin

g to elide | `🥗 on` |
| After a pass | `🥗 −1.9k /req · 286.0k saved` |
| A tool had to be re-fetched

| `… ↺3` |
| `mode: always` | `… ⚠ mode always` |

`−x /req` is what the current surface saves on every request; `y saved` is the
cumulative total over

the session; `↺n` counts re-fetches. The footer hides itself
when `enabled: false` or `showStatus:

ssion; `↺n` counts re-fetches. The footer hides itself
when `enabled: false` or `showStatus: false`.
## Protection: what is never elided
The gates are the upstream ones, in the upstream order:
| Gate | Rule |
| Cache warmth | Only when the last assistant message is **strictly older** than `cacheTtlMinutes`;

no timestamp means never. |
| Recency | Results from the last `keepTurns` assistant turns stay. |
|

Size | Results below `minChars` stay. |
| Errors | `keepErrors: true` (default) keeps every failed r

esult, whatever its size. |
| Tools | `neverElide` names are never touched. |
| Rich content | Image

s, attachments and any non-plain-text block are never touched. |
| Growth | A stub must be strictly

smaller than what it shadows, or the replacement is refused. |
| Re-fetch feedback | When an identic
al call is re-issued after elision it is counted; at more than `recoveryThreshold` of a tool's elide

d results (with at least 5 samples) that tool is protected for the rest of the session. |
| Failure
| Any error in the pre-step fails open: the turn continues untouched. |
## Commands
| Command | Effect |

| `/context-diet` | Status: settings, per-request and cumulative savings, cold starts, recovery. |
|

`/context-diet show` | What is elided now, and what the next cold start would take. |
| `/context-d

iet on` / `off` | Toggle for this session. |
| `/context-diet now` | One pass on the next step, acce

pting one cache rewrite. |
| `/context-diet keep <1-500>` | Keep the last N turns for this session.

|
| `/context-diet ttl <1-1440>` | Cache lifetime in minutes, for this session. |
| `/context-diet m
ode <cold\|always>` | `always` ignores the cold gate (only for providers without prompt caching). |
| `/context-diet args <on\|off>` | Reports the platform limit below; arguments are always kept on DS
context-diet args <on\|off>` | Reports the platform limit below; arguments are always kept on DSH. |

Command changes are **session-scoped**. DSH keeps plugin configuration in the
profile Config, so a c
ommand never rewrites it and never reloads the plugin.
## Configuration
| Key | Default | Meaning |

| `enabled` | `true` | Master switch. |
| `mode` | `"cold"` | `cold`: elide only when the prompt cac

he expired (free). `always`: ignore coldness. |
| `keepTurns` | `20` | Keep the results of the last

N assistant turns. |
| `minChars` | `1500` | Results smaller than this are not worth a stub. |
| `ca

cheTtlMinutes` | `5` | Prompt-cache lifetime; a longer idle period means cold. |
| `keepErrors` | `t

rue` | Keep results flagged as errors. |
| `neverElide` | `[]` | Tool names that are never elided. |

| `showStatus` | `true` | Render the composer footer. |
| `stubTailLines` | `3` | Tail lines kept i

n a stub. |
| `stubErrorLines` | `3` | Error lines kept in a stub. |
| `autoProtect` | `true` | Prot

ect a tool whose results keep being re-fetched. |
| `recoveryThreshold` | `0.25` | Re-fetch share th
at triggers protection (0.05-1). |

`elideArgs` is not a config key: the adapter pins it to `false` and the
`/context-diet/stats` payloa

d reports that pinned value, so `status` and the footer
agree about what the plugin actually does.
A config override replaces the whole `config` block, so restate every key you keep:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
## Durable surface: what changes
| Surface | Effect |
| Model-visible session surface | Old plain-text results become stubs, durably, for this session. |

| Session event log | Append-only; the original events are still there. |
| Human transcript | Uncha

nged: replacements are model-only. |
| Token accounting | Corrected by the `compaction/prune` shadow

price; no private estimator. |
| Other sessions | Untouched. |
## Security

- Host code runs in-process, outside the workspace sandbox: install only from a
source you trust.
-

The Client reads the same-origin `/context-diet/stats` endpoint. It writes
nothing, and the endpoint

refuses unauthenticated requests.
- No lifecycle scripts, no install-time downloads, no direct `$DS

H_HOME` access,
no filesystem scan and no subprocess.
